candidates.source_name: Cyril of Alexandria / Commentary on the Psalms
candidates.source_attribution: Cyril of Alexandria, on Psalm 22/23 (LXX numbering). NPNF Series 2, vol. 7. PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Cyril of Alexandria Commentary on the Psalms (c. 428 AD)

Cyril reads 'The Lord is my shepherd' Christologically: the shepherd of Psalm 23 is the same as the Good Shepherd of John 10, the same as the Lamb of Revelation. The 'I shall not want' is a confession of complete dependence on the Incarnate Word who is at once Lamb and Shepherd. Tewahedo liturgy preserves this Christological reading prominently in the burial office.

candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / Epistola ad Marcellinum §3
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistola ad Marcellinum de Interpretatione Psalmorum (Letter to Marcellinus on the Interpretation of the Psalms), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 27 (1857). The Letter is Athanasius's principal pastoral-spiritual work — a personal letter to Marcellinus (recovering from illness) explaining how to use each Psalm as prayer for specific spiritual circumstances. Hermeneutic anchor for the Tewahedo Office (Säʿatat) Psalter-recitation tradition.
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Epistola ad Marcellinum §3 (c. 350 AD)

'The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want' (LXX 22:1 — kyrios poimainei me kai ouden me hysterēsei) — Athanasius marks Ps 23 (LXX 22) as the PARADIGMATIC PASTORAL-COMFORT-PSALM in the Letter to Marcellinus: prescribed for the soul-tending-toward-providential-trust. The kyrios poimainei me (the Lord shepherds-me) is read Christologically — the Word-incarnate is the Johannine ho poimēn ho kalos (the Good Shepherd, Jn 10:11). The Athanasian pastoral-spiritual hermeneutic transforms the Psalter into a Christic-prayer-book: each Psalm voices a stance-toward-Christ that the praying-soul takes-up. The Tewahedo Säʿatat (Liturgy of the Hours) Psalter-pattern preserves this Athanasian pastoral-Psalter use.
